deck_title: Huygens-Steiner I = I_cm + m*d^2 parallel-axis moment of inertia vs naive unshifted CoM inertia rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Christiaan Huygens (1673) & Jakob Steiner (1834) parallel-axis moment-of-inertia theorem (shifting the rotation axis by distance d from the center of mass increases rotational inertia to I_pivot = I_cm + m * d^2 = I_cm * (1 + (d/k_g)^2) = I_cm * (1 + u), locking I_exact / I_model = 1.0000x across all 17 pivot-offset stations u = (d/k_g)^2 in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive unshifted centroidal inertia (I = I_cm, which underestimates inertia and overshoots angular acceleration alpha = tau / I by 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-element shifted mass-volume quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Ragdoll limb joints, warhammer/greatsword grip swings, hinged heavy doors, trebuchet counterweights, and compound pendulum animations
Adding the parallel-axis tensor m * ((d·d)I_3 - d ⊗ d) whenever a rigid body rotates about an off-center joint or grip point
Computing exact Huygens center-of-oscillation length L_eq = k_g^2 / d + d for physical pendulum period matching
not_for: Free-floating satellites in zero gravity rotating strictly about their own center of mass (d = 0)
Pure translational particle emitters with no rotational degrees of freedom
